T1.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare parallel work decomposition while preserving the requested thread budget: worksharing the independent coarse-root tiles (including static versus dynamic scheduling) and parallelizing the independent base-level depth-bound rows in MinMaxZTree::Update. Measure each approach independently and, if useful, measure a combination rather than assuming additive gains; higher tree levels still depend on completed lower levels. Keep culling and shading algorithms unchanged, pass run()'s thread count as an upper bound, avoid unnecessary overhead at one thread, and preserve disjoint writes. Validate full output and correctness at 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
T1.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget

T2.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing recursive culling and hierarchy work in MinMaxZTree, SplitTileMinMax, IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax, and traversal. In addition to tile granularity and conservative plane-test optimizations, compare stopping subdivision for tiles with small nonzero light lists against continuing to the leaves; measure saved traversal/culling against the added per-pixel light work. Preserve conservative culling, current-frame depth-bound recomputation, and correctness for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Do not add parallelism or change ShadeTileC in this branch. Validate both core counts and altered light colors.
T2.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead

T3.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
T3.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization

mission.hypothesis: Each shaded pixel repeats indirect gathers through the same tile light-index list into separate light arrays, and recomputes invariant attenuation-end squared and attenuation range terms. A per-tile packed cache should amortize those loads and calculations while preserving the original per-pixel BRDF operations and light colors. This tests cache/preparation overhead versus reuse; the catalog has no earlier T3 candidates, and the baseline does not provide separate 1- and 4-core timings.

retained: Pack each tile's referenced light positions, attenuation values, and color channels into a local cache once before shading its pixels.
Precompute each light's attenuation-end square and attenuation range once, reusing the same float operations and leaving per-pixel normalization, powf, and BRDF evaluation unchanged.

mission.hypothesis: Stopping subdivision when a tile has 1–3 lights should reduce recursive culling work while bounding the added per-pixel light loop to three candidates; light-count visualization retains leaf-level behavior. Skipping XY plane tests when every child fails the conservative Z tests should further reduce split work. Ceiling tile counts, clipping edge-tile depth scans, and rebuilding the tree on dimension changes preserve correctness beyond evenly divisible layouts. These are hypotheses, not measured gains.

Skip split-plane calculations when conservative Z tests reject all four children.
Use ceiling tile counts, clip edge-tile depth scans, and rebuild the hierarchy if framebuffer dimensions change.

mission.hypothesis: The serial coarse-root loop may leave cores idle when recursive shading workloads differ by tile. This candidate tests dynamic one-tile work assignment across root tiles, with run()'s thread count as the cap; the serial path is retained for one thread. It does not parallelize depth-bound rows, so its effect can be evaluated independently of that approach.

hypotheses.claim: Le parallélisme des lignes de base pourrait compléter le travail sur les tuiles, mais son apport indépendant et celui d’une combinaison ne sont pas établis.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Comparer séparément, à 1 et 4 cœurs, la variante actuelle, le parallélisme des lignes de base, puis leur combinaison; vérifier la sortie complète, y compris avec couleurs de lumière modifiées. Confirmer la meilleure variante avec les 5 répétitions prévues.
hypotheses.stop_condition: Écarter toute variante incorrecte; arrêter cette piste si la variante lignes seules n’améliore pas le temps moyen confirmé de l’essai validé (0,06258 s), sans présumer d’un gain additif.

observations.claim: Mesures visibles : baseline valide et correcte à 0,11495 s (score 0,5); essai T1 valide et correct à 0,06258 s (score 0,64751). L’essai T1 a un temps moyen observé inférieur au baseline, sans attribution causale possible ici.
Un résultat de développement est marqué valide et correct, mais sans temps ni score mesurés.

uncertainties: Le code source et les pages de preuve détaillées ne sont pas visibles ici; impossible d’identifier l’ordonnancement effectivement essayé ou de comparer séparément tuiles et lignes.
Les détails de validation par nombre de cœurs et avec couleurs modifiées, ainsi que la dispersion des mesures, manquent.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied original scalar renderer on AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Render the supplied 1280x720 deferred-lighting frame, preserving all lights, geometry and shading. InputData and Framebuffer types are in include/deferred.h. Write all r/g/b uint8 framebuffer planes; tolerance at most one intensity level per component. Performance 1 and 4 cores, checks also alter light colors. Do not cache rendered frames; reusable scratch storage is allowed, with current-frame depth bounds and lighting recomputed on each invocation.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Preserve extern C void run(RenderInput*,float*image,int*ids,int threads). The include/ files document the ABI and are immutable. Respect threads as the maximum CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only. Fully overwrite the specified output on every call. No cached answers, external libraries, file/network access, timing or environment inspection, phase detection, hardcoded output or changes to the protected protocol. C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Allocation inside run is timed. The timing excludes input generation, oracle and compilation. The optimized ISPC reference implementation is withheld. Explore independent topics, record failed trials, integrate memory and independently confirm final G.
